prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a narrow entryway with closed double wooden doors directly in front of the camera wearer (about 0.5–1.0 m away at eye level) and a low cabinet to the right (0.6–1.2 m away), both above a tiled floor approximately 1.5–1.7 m below the head-mounted camera where the wearer's own legs and shoes are visible at the bottom. In frames 2 and 3, the wearer's right arm extends forward from the bottom right (<0.3 m) to reach the metal door latch (0.5–0.7 m away), partially occluding the right door panel and cabinet, before retracting in frame 4 as the camera wearer approaches slightly closer to the upper door panels. In frame 5, the left and right door panels swing open inward to frame a second person standing in the threshold about 1.0–1.5 m ahead and 0.4 m behind the wearer's raised right hand, with that person's head cropped out above the top edge of the view. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map clearly separates the foreground raised arm from the cabinet and floor shadow without lighting ambiguity, though it is unreliable in frame 3 and 4 where the upper door panels become over-saturated as nearer than the floor and in frame 5 where the open doorway and the standing person's legs blend into a dark, poorly differentiated far-depth region.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map fails completely in frame 1 (returning an all-black mask), then in frame 2 segments the camera wearer's extended right arm on the right (~0.3–0.6 m away), right leg at the bottom center (~1.2–1.5 m below the camera), and left hand holding an object at the bottom left as separate `person` instances, while misclassifying the closed left door panel in front (~0.8–1.0 m away) as a `chair` and the right cabinet plus right door (~0.6–1.2 m away, 0.2 m right of the door seam) as a `laptop`. In frame 3, a single `person` mask unites the wearer's extended right arm reaching the latch (0.5 m away, within arm's reach) and lower leg at the bottom, and in frame 4 only the wearer's lower leg remains segmented at the bottom center as the arm retreats out of view. By frame 5, as the doors open to either side, a single continuous `person` mask merges the camera wearer's raised foreground right arm with the newly visible second person standing upright in front (~1.0–1.5 m away, facing toward the camera wearer with their head and feet occluded by the top border and the wearer's hand). While the masks in frames 2–5 help isolate human limbs from the cluttered floor and shadows in RGB, the map is highly unreliable because it misses all doors, shoes, and walls in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5, severely mislabels the door and cabinet in frame 2, and merges two distinct people at different depths into one instance in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 through 4, detecting no body or hand skeletons for the camera wearer's visible lower legs, left hand, or extended right arm reaching within arm's reach (0.5–0.7 m) of the door latch. In frame 5, when the double doors open, a yellow partial body skeleton appears in the upper-right quadrant for the second person standing about 1.0–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer between the open door panels, along with a magenta hand skeleton just below it (~0.5–0.8 m away). The yellow keypoints trace the standing person's left and right wrists and hips (about 0.3–0.4 m apart horizontally), confirming their torso faces directly toward the camera wearer with both arms hanging down within reach of the door edges, while their head and shoulders remain cut off above the top of the frame so gaze direction cannot be observed. Just below the standing person's hip line, the magenta hand skeleton captures the camera wearer's raised right hand (roughly 0.4–0.5 m in front of the other person's legs and partially occluding their feet), making the finger articulation clearer than in the motion-blurred RGB frame, though the map is unreliable in missing all limbs in frames 1–4 and erroneously placing isolated yellow body dots on the wearer's hand in frame 5.
